newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian cotton prices steady on more export hopes.
newsitem.headline: Indian cotton prices steady on more export hopes.

text.p: Indian cotton prices held steady on Thursday on hopes more export of cotton would be allowed by the authorities, dealers said.
"Mill buying was low. But offerings were limited on expectations that Indian government may allow more export of cotton next month," one dealer said.
The government has so far allowed export of about 10 million bales (170 kg each) for the 1996/97 season and traders expect another 250,000/300,000 bales to be allowed for export.

Reports of rising new crop arrivals in producing centres had little impact on the market. In spot deals Bengal-deshi was quiet at 770/825 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) while Punjab saw-ginned was steady at 1,390/1,610 rupees per maund. Gujarat varieties too remained quiet.
